a51_new: On a 16-place grid, where the calmest state can be found exactly, that state sits far below the background; A53 traced this to how the small grid wraps around (next bullet).
a53_bullet: - **The small-grid result was a quirk of wrapping; the background now leads on large grids (A53; the wrapping checked by me).** On the 16-place grid, wrapping around makes each place meet one partner six times over at distance two, and the exact calmest state simply locks those pairs together (exact). A 24-place grid has the same kind of quirk through doubled diagonal links: its lowest state found lies well below the background and is built from those doubled links. On grids of 216, 512 and 1,000 places, rivals built exactly from locked groups of 2 to 18 places all lose to the background, by 0.04 to 0.06 per place, and blending the background toward them only raises its energy (checked). A rough estimate for loosely linked cubes comes within about 0.005 per place, so that contest is still open. So under its best farther-reaching rule the half-particle background is the best state found on large grids, but not yet shown to be the calmest.
